svg.title: Slide the gradients into the window, then slide them back
svg.desc: A hand-drawn logarithmic magnitude axis from 1e-10 to 1e5 with a wide dashed BF16 band above it and a narrower hachured FP16 band from 6.1e-5 to 65504, a histogram of gradient magnitudes sitting mostly to the left of the FP16 band in red with 47 percent rounding to zero, a fat amber arrow multiplying by 65536 to move the histogram inside the band leaving 0.02 percent lost, a return arrow for unscaling, a crossed-out clip-before-unscale box, and bars comparing 1,381 against 2,918 images per second.
svg.text: Slide the gradients into the window, then slide them back
same exponent range as fp32, three fewer mantissa bits
47% of gradients round straight to zero
clips the SCALED gradients. It trains,
bf16 needs no scaler at all. If your GPU is
Ampere or newer, just use bf16 and delete
...and if 16 bits is fine, why not 8? -> Week 26
